I am thinking...: Now I have a clear understanding. Let me analyze the vulnerability logic and build a local ASAN harness to confirm the crash.
Vulnerability analysis:

The admonition special-case gate in md_process_line (md4c.c lines 6530-6551):
```c
if((ctx->parser.flags & MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS) &&
   ctx->current_block == NULL && ctx->n_block_bytes >= (int)sizeof(MD_BLOCK))
{
    MD_BLOCK* block = (MD_BLOCK*)((char*)ctx->block_bytes + ctx->n_block_bytes - sizeof(MD_BLOCK));
    if(block->type == MD_BLOCK_QUOTE && line->end - line->beg > 3 && line->end - line->beg < 16 &&
       CH(line->beg) == _T('[') && CH(line->beg+1) == _T('!') && CH(line->end-1) == _T(']'))
    {
        ...
        MD_ASSERT(ctx->n_containers > 0 && ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1].ch == _T('>'));
        ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1].is_admonition = TRUE;   // line 6544
```

The gate checks `block->type == MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` (the LAST block in block_bytes) but does NOT verify there is an active quote container (n_containers > 0 with ch=='>'). The MD_ASSERT is compiled out in release/ASAN builds.

Trigger path: After a block quote container is CLOSED, md_leave_child_containers pushes an MD_BLOCK_QUOTE CLOSER (type==MD_BLOCK_QUOTE) to block_bytes and decrements n_containers to 0. If current_block==NULL and the next line is an admonition tag like `[!NOTE]` at top level (no `>`), the gate matches the QUOTE closer and reads ctx->containers[n_containers-1] = ctx->containers[-1] => heap-buffer-overflow read.

PoC markdown:
```
> text

[!NOTE]
```
- Line 1 `> text`: enters quote container (n_containers=1, QUOTE opener pushed), starts P block.
- Line 2 blank: analyze_line leaves quote container (pushes QUOTE closer, n_containers=0); process_line ends P block (current_block=NULL). Last block in block_bytes = QUOTE closer.
- Line 3 `[!NOTE]`: analyze_line: n_containers=0, no container, TEXT. process_line: gate fires (current_block==NULL, last block type==MD_BLOCK_QUOTE, line matches admonition) -> reads ctx->containers[-1] OOB.

The fuzz harness fuzz-mdhtml.c consumes 8 header bytes (parser_flags, renderer_flags) then markdown. parser_flags must include MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS (0x80000).

So candidate bytes = LE32(0x80000) + LE32(0) + "> text\n\n[!NOTE]\n".

Let me build with ASAN to confirm.

Now I have a good understanding of the vulnerability. Let me think about the bug carefully.

The vulnerability is in `md_process_line` at the admonition special-case gate (lines 6530-6551). The gate checks:
- `ctx->parser.flags & MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS`
- `ctx->current_block == NULL`
- `ctx->n_block_bytes >= (int)sizeof(MD_BLOCK)`

Then it gets the last block:
```c
MD_BLOCK* block = (MD_BLOCK*)((char*)ctx->block_bytes + ctx->n_block_bytes - sizeof(MD_BLOCK));
```

And checks `block->type == MD_BLOCK_QUOTE`. If true, and the line looks like an admonition tag `[!NOTE]` etc., then:
```c
MD_ASSERT(ctx->n_containers > 0  &&  ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1].ch == _T('>'));
ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1].is_admonition = TRUE;
```

The issue: the gate checks that the last block is `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE`, but it does NOT check that there's an active quote container (`ctx->n_containers > 0` with `ch == '>'`). The `MD_ASSERT` is only active in debug builds. In a release build, if `ctx->n_containers == 0`, then `ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1]` = `ctx->containers[-1]` which is an out-of-bounds read (heap-buffer-overflow read).

So the question is: how can we have `block->type == MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` in the block_bytes buffer while `ctx->n_containers == 0` (no active quote container)?

Let me think about how `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` gets into `block_bytes`. Looking at `md_enter_child_containers`:
```c
case _T('>'):
    MD_CHECK(md_push_container_bytes(ctx, MD_BLOCK_QUOTE, 0, 0, MD_BLOCK_CONTAINER_OPENER));
    break;
```

So when a `>` container is entered, an `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` opener is pushed to block_bytes. And `md_push_container` adds to `ctx->containers`.

Now, the block_bytes buffer holds both container openers/closers AND leaf blocks. The admonition gate looks at the LAST block in block_bytes (`ctx->n_block_bytes - sizeof(MD_BLOCK)`).

Wait, but the gate requires `ctx->current_block == NULL`. `current_block` is the current leaf block being built. So when `current_block == NULL`, the last block in block_bytes could be a container opener (like `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` opener) or a container closer, or a leaf block that was just ended.

Hmm, let me think about the scenario. The admonition gate fires when:
1. `current_block == NULL` (no active leaf block)
2. The last block in block_bytes is `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE`
3. The line is an admonition tag like `[!NOTE]`

But there's no check that `ctx->n_containers > 0` and the top container is a quote.

When would the last block be `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` but `n_containers == 0`? 

The `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` opener is pushed when entering a quote container. The `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` closer is pushed when leaving. After the closer, `n_containers` is decremented (in `md_process_all_blocks`, not during line processing). Wait, no.

Actually, let me re-examine. During line processing (`md_process_doc`), `ctx->containers` is the active container stack. `md_push_container`/`md_leave_child_containers` modify `ctx->n_containers` during line analysis. The block_bytes buffer gets container opener/closer bytes pushed via `md_push_container_bytes` during `md_enter_child_containers`/`md_leave_child_containers`.

So during line processing, `ctx->n_containers` reflects the currently active containers. When a quote container is left via `md_leave_child_containers`, `ctx->n_containers` is decremented AND an `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` closer is pushed to block_bytes.

Hmm, so after leaving a quote, the last block in block_bytes would be the `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` closer, and `n_containers` would be decremented. But the closer has `MD_BLOCK_CONTAINER_CLOSER` flag, not opener. The admonition gate only checks `block->type == MD_BLOCK_QUOTE`, not the opener/closer flag!

Wait, but actually let me reconsider. Let me re-read the gate:

```c
if((ctx->parser.flags & MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS)  &&
   ctx->current_block == NULL  &&  ctx->n_block_bytes >= (int)sizeof(MD_BLOCK))
{
    MD_BLOCK* block = (MD_BLOCK*)((char*)ctx->block_bytes + ctx->n_block_bytes - sizeof(MD_BLOCK));

    if(block->type == MD_BLOCK_QUOTE  &&  line->end - line->beg > 3  &&  line->end - line->beg < 16 &&
       CH(line->beg) == _T('[')  &&  CH(line->beg+1) == _T('!')  &&  CH(line->end-1) == _T(']'))
    {
        ...
        MD_ASSERT(ctx->n_containers > 0  &&  ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1].ch == _T('>'));
        ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1].is_admonition = TRUE;
```

So the gate fires when the last block in block_bytes is `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` (either opener or closer, since it doesn't check the flag). 

Now, the normal admonition case: `> [!NOTE]`. Let's trace:
- Line 1: `> [!NOTE]`. `md_analyze_line` sees `>` container mark, pushes a quote container (`n_containers` becomes 1), and pushes `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` opener to block_bytes. Then the rest `[!NOTE]` is text. So `line->type = MD_LINE_TEXT`, `line->beg` points to `[!NOTE]`.

How? The `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` closer. When a quote container is closed, `md_leave_child_containers` pushes an `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` closer (type `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` with `MD_BLOCK_CONTAINER_CLOSER` flag) and decrements `n_containers`. The gate checks `block->type == MD_BLOCK_QUOTE` (the LAST block in block_bytes) but does NOT verify there is an active quote container (n_containers > 0 with ch=='>'). The MD_ASSERT is compiled out in release/ASAN builds.

Trigger path: After a block quote container is CLOSED, md_leave_child_containers pushes an MD_BLOCK_QUOTE CLOSER (type==MD_BLOCK_QUOTE) to block_bytes and decrements n_containers to 0. If current_block==NULL and the next line is an admonition tag like `[!NOTE]` at top level (no `>`), the gate matches the QUOTE closer and reads ctx->containers[n_containers-1] = ctx->containers[-1] => heap-buffer-overflow read.

PoC markdown:
```
> text

[!NOTE]
```
- Line 1 `> text`: enters quote container (n_containers=1, QUOTE opener pushed), starts P block.
- Line 2 blank: analyze_line leaves quote container (pushes QUOTE closer, n_containers=0); process_line ends P block (current_block=NULL). Last block in block_bytes = QUOTE closer.
- Line 3 `[!NOTE]`: analyze_line: n_containers=0, no container, TEXT. process_line: gate fires (current_block==NULL, last block type==MD_BLOCK_QUOTE, line matches admonition) -> reads ctx->containers[-1] OOB.

The fuzz harness fuzz-mdhtml.c consumes 8 header bytes (parser_flags, renderer_flags) then markdown. parser_flags must include MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS (0x80000).

So candidate bytes = LE32(0x80000) + LE32(0) + "> text\n\n[!NOTE]\n".
